added.member: CSS alignment-baseline, baseline-shift, baseline-source and dominant-baseline
added.summary: vertical-align is CSS Inline 3's shorthand of alignment-baseline, baseline-shift and baseline-source, and all four properties and dominant-baseline apply to text runs and inline-level boxes. A run aligns its alphabetic, ideographic, central, middle, mathematical, hanging, text-top or text-bottom baseline (`baseline`: its paragraph's dominant-baseline) with the same baseline of the paragraph's text, from each font's BASE table or the baselines CSS Inline 3 Appendix A.2 synthesizes; baseline-shift then raises it by a length, a percentage of its line height, sub or super, or places it on the line box's top, centre or bottom. SVG text's dominant-baseline takes the same font baselines.

fixed.member: CSS vertical-align on an inline block
fixed.summary: An inline block aligns by its last baseline (baseline-source: auto, CSS 2.1 §10.8.1): a two-line inline block beside text sits with its second line on the text's baseline, not its first. baseline-source: first keeps the first. A table cell's vertical-align: text-top and text-bottom place its content at the start and end.
